blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Epidemiological evidence indicates that leptospirosis hospital admissions tend to peak about two weeks after heavy rains, with flooding considered one of the “critical drivers” of transmission. A peer-reviewed study by the Polytechnic University of the Philippines, published in Emerging Infectious Diseases, said the country often sees leptospirosis outbreaks several weeks after Habagat-triggered flooding. For instance, in 2025, the Department of Health (DOH) recorded 3,037 leptospirosis cases from January to July, with 1,114 occurring within a week after the start of the rainy season.
